findings.current: “……He’s got good ears. Fine, just come sit down.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the implied subject from Cheongpung, whom the porter is addressing, to a third-person remark about him.
findings.rationale: 귀가 밝구먼 directly comments on Cheongpung’s sharp hearing before telling him to come sit down.
findings.replacement: “……You’ve got sharp ears. Fine, just come sit down.”

findings.current: “How have you lasted nearly a month with someone like him beside you?”
findings.defect: The draft reverses the duration: 달포 is a little over a month, not less than one month.
findings.rationale: 달포 denotes a period slightly longer than a month, while “nearly a month” denotes less than a month.
findings.replacement: “How have you lasted over a month with someone like him beside you?”
findings.source: “어떻게 이런 놈을 옆에 끼고 달포씩이나 버티셨소?”

findings.defect: The porter is asking what kind of person Cheongpung is, not what activity he is currently performing.
findings.rationale: 뭐 하는 놈 in this context questions Cheongpung’s character or background after his bizarre reply.

findings.defect: The declarative English loses the contrasting, mildly puzzled response conveyed by -는데요.
findings.rationale: Cheongpung is casually contradicting their assumption that his life must have been difficult, and that pragmatic contrast is part of the humor.

findings.current: “Yes. I ended up making a wasted trip somehow, but I don’t mind it even now. This escort work is pretty interesting, too.”
findings.defect: The draft makes 지금도 나쁘지 않아요 mean that Cheongpung still does not mind the wasted trip; the source says his present circumstances are not bad despite that wasted trip.
findings.rationale: 지금도 refers to his current situation, which he immediately illustrates by saying that escort work is interesting.
findings.replacement: “Yes. It turned out to be a wasted trip, but… things aren’t bad now, either. This escort work is pretty interesting, too.”
findings.source: “네. 어쩌다 보니 헛걸음을 하게 됐는데…… 지금도 나쁘지 않아요. 표행이란 것도 상당히 재밌어요.”

findings.current: Besides, he had lived in the mountains his entire life as the son of a slash-and-burn farmer. It made sense that he would feel this way.
findings.defect: The draft invents a parent-child identity. The source says Seokchil believes Cheongpung himself comes from a slash-and-burn farming background, not specifically that his parent was such a farmer.
findings.rationale: 화전민 출신 identifies Cheongpung’s presumed background; it does not identify his father or mother.
findings.replacement: Besides, he had lived in the mountains his entire life and came from a slash-and-burn farming community. It made sense that he would feel this way.
findings.source: 더군다나 평생 산에서 살아온 화전민 출신이니 그럴 법도 하다.

findings.current: Cheongpung pulled a yellowish bamboo slip from inside his clothes and handed it over.
findings.defect: The draft changes the physical action from showing the contract to handing it over.
findings.rationale: 보여 줬다 means he displayed or showed the slip; the source reserves an explicit handing-over action for the silver ingots later.
findings.replacement: Cheongpung pulled a yellowish bamboo slip from inside his clothes and showed it to them.
findings.source: 청풍이 품에서 누리끼리한 죽간 하나를 꺼내어 보여 줬다.

findings.current: “Does it mean I have to pay with my body?”
findings.defect: The literal wording introduces a strong sexual implication absent from the Korean euphemism.
findings.rationale: 몸으로 때우다 here means discharging the debt through labor or bodily service rather than paying money; it is not a sexual proposition.
findings.replacement: “Does it mean I’d have to work it off?”

findings.current: It was then that Seokchil’s eyes nearly rolled back in his head.
findings.defect: The draft renders the Korean anger idiom as a literal physical symptom suggestive of fainting or seizure.
findings.rationale: 눈이 뒤집히다 in this context means becoming enraged or losing control, not literally rolling one’s eyes backward.
findings.replacement: It was just then, as Seokchil was about to snap.

findings.current: “When I left home, my family gave me some traveling money.”
findings.defect: The draft supplies Cheongpung’s family as the giver even though the source deliberately omits who gave him the money.
findings.rationale: 받았거든요 states only that Cheongpung received the money. The following narration speculates about his household, so the dialogue should not prematurely resolve the giver.
findings.replacement: “I was given some traveling money when I left home.”

summary: The draft contains several altered subjects, quantities, actions, and implied identities, along with a euphemism made misleadingly explicit.
